newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Hambro Insurance sees slower H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Hambro Insurance sees slower H2.

text.p: Heavy hurricane billings blew interim profits sharply higher at Hambro Insurance Services Group Plc but were not expected to provide a similar windfall in the second half, a top executive said on Thursday.

Managing director Nicholas Page told Reuters that Hambro's first-half pretax profits swelled 49 percent to 4.53 million stg, including a 1.0 million stg contribution from claims arising from last year's busy hurricane season.
The company, which advises insurers on claims, posted pretax profits of 3.03 million stg in the year-ago period.

"The vast majority of those hurricane billings have now been done," he said. "We did get some hurricanes this year in the Caribbean, particularly hurricanes Bertha and Hortense. But they're nothing like the same magnitide."
Page said the high number of claims in the first six months ended Sept 30 would decrease the company's second-half bias, which normally runs at a ratio of about two-to-one.
"We have a second-half bias because most of our business is in northern Europe, and you get more claims in the winter than in the summer," he said.
Analysts currently expect the company to make a pretax profit about 11 million stg for the year, Page said, declining comment on the forecast.
The company, which is 53-percent-owned by investment bank Hambros Plc, reported profits of 11.1 million last year, including a high number of hurricane billings.
Regarding recent pressure on the parent to increase shareholder value, Page said Hambros had given no indication it planned to divest Hambro.
"All I can tell you is that everything that Hambros has said to us is they're delighted with Hambro Insurance Services. And as far as I am aware, there is no change," he said.
He added that Hambro's first-half results reflected the continued recovery of its loss-adjusting group, while its Hambro Legal Protection still faced strong competitive pressures.
Hambro also said its Beale Dobie business was well placed to benefit from strong investment demand in the second-half.
The company's shares edged up 1/2p to 92p in morning trade.
